articles.title: YAP Fuels Cerebral Cavernous Malformations by Regulating KLF4 Transcriptional Activity and Protein Stability.
articles.abstract: Cerebral cavernous malformations (CCMs), which frequently predispose patients to strokes or seizures, primarily arise from endothelial specific loss-of-function mutations in the CCM genes, and occasionally accompanied by gain-of-function mutations in PIK3CA and MAP3K3. While the Hippo pathway is a well-established regulator of tissue homeostasis, its emerging relevance in vascular pathology particularly its precise role in CCM pathogenesis remains poorly understood. In this study, we demonstrate that CCM gene deficiency suppresses endothelial Hippo signaling, as evidenced by diminished LATS activity, alongside concomitant elevation of YAP expression and nuclear translocation in both human and mouse CCM lesions. Notably, endothelial-specific deletion of Yap mitigates CCM lesion formation, reinforces endothelial junctions, enhances inflammatory resistance, and decreases KLF4 protein levels in a CCM mouse model. Conversely, intracranial Adeno-associated virus (AAV)-mediated inhibition of LATS or activation of YAP promoted CCMs formation under Ccm2 deficiency. Mechanistically, under the dual coordination of negative regulation by LATS and positive regulation by MAP3K3, YAP orchestrates KLF4 transcriptional activity and protein stability. This is achieved through a direct interaction with KLF4 that shields it from β-TrCP-mediated proteasomal degradation, thereby driving CCM progression. Collectively, our findings unveil a novel dimension to Hippo pathway regulation and underscore YAP as a pivotal driver of CCM pathogenesis.

articles.title: Xijiao Dihuang decoction attenuates microglia/macrophage-mediated inflammatory response in cerebral injury by modulating the PI3K/Akt/HIF-1α/NLRP3 axis.
articles.abstract:
ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Xijiao Dihuang Decoction (XJDH), originating from Beiji Qianjin Yaofang (Thousand Gold Prescriptions for Emergencies) compiled by Sun Simiao during the Tang Dynasty (652 AD), is a classical Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) formula comprising Cornu Bubali (substituted for Rhinoceros horn), Radix Rehmanniae, Paeoniae Radix Rubra, and Cortex Moutan. In TCM clinical practice, XJDH has traditionally been prescribed for "Xue-Re" (Blood-Heat) syndrome characterized by febrile diseases with bleeding tendency, blood stasis and impaired consciousness, a clinical pattern that shares pathophysiological features with the inflammatory cascade and microcirculatory dysfunction in acute ischemic stroke (AIS). However, the molecular mechanism by which XJDH alleviates cerebral injury via the microglia/macrophage inflammatory cascade remains incompletely characterized.
AIM OF THE STUDY: This study aims to elucidate the mechanism by which XJDH ameliorates cerebral injury by mitigating the microglia/macrophage inflammatory cascade, in association with the PI3K/Akt/HIF-1α/NLRP3 axis.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: The middle cerebral artery occlusion (MCAO) model in C57BL/6 J mice and a lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-induced inflammatory model in RAW264.7 and THP-1 cells were established for in vivo and in vitro experiments, respectively. Pathological alterations, inflammatory responses, and the PI3K/Akt/HIF-1α axis were assessed by HE staining, TUNEL assay, immunofluorescence, ELISA, RT-qPCR, and Western blot analyses. The PI3K inhibitor LY294002, the Akt agonist SC79 and the HIF-1α agonist DMOG were employed for pathway verification. Serum from 60 participants (20 controls, 20 AIS, and 20 AIS treated with XJDH) was also analyzed for inflammatory cytokines.
RESULTS: XJDH dose-dependently promoted neurological function, decreased cerebral infarct volume, attenuated histopathological injury, and mitigated cell apoptosis in MCAO. Network pharmacology identified 244 shared targets between XJDH and AIS, with PI3K/Akt and HIF-1 pathways ranking among the top enriched pathways. Molecular docking confirmed favorable binding affinities of key XJDH constituents to PI3K (-8.7 kcal/mol), Akt (-6.0 kcal/mol), and HIF-1α (-7.0 kcal/mol). XJDH significantly enhanced PI3K and Akt phosphorylation levels, downregulated HIF-1α and NLRP3, and shifted microglia/macrophages from an M1-toward an M2-dominant phenotype in MCAO mice. These effects were largely abolished by LY294002 in both RAW264.7 and THP-1 cells. Consistently, Akt activation by SC79 potentiated, whereas HIF-1α stabilization by DMOG reversed, the anti-inflammatory effect of XJDH, supporting the involvement of the Akt-HIF-1α axis.
CONCLUSIONS: XJDH ameliorates cerebral injury in mice in association with the PI3K/Akt/HIF-1α/NLRP3 axis and a shift of microglia/macrophages away from an M1-dominant phenotype; these findings provide preclinical, ethnopharmacology-oriented rationale warranting further validation in neuron-macrophage co-culture systems and, ultimately, randomized clinical evaluation.

articles.title: Integrated network analysis, proteomics, and experimental validation reveal the mechanisms underlying the renoprotective effects of salvianolic acid A against diabetic nephropathy.
articles.abstract:
ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Salvianolic acid A (SAA), a major bioactive constituent of Salvia miltiorrhiza, has attracted considerable attention because of its diverse pharmacological activities in metabolic and vascular disorders. Diabetic nephropathy (DN) is one of the most serious microvascular complications of diabetes and remains a leading cause of end-stage renal disease worldwide. Although increasing evidence has demonstrated the renoprotective effects of SAA, the precise molecular mechanisms underlying its therapeutic actions in DN remain incompletely understood.
AIM OF THE STUDY: This study aimed to systematically investigate the therapeutic mechanisms of SAA against DN by integrating network pharmacology, quantitative proteomics, molecular docking, and experimental validation.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: Potential therapeutic targets and signaling pathways of SAA in DN were identified through network pharmacology and quantitative proteomic analyses. A high-fat diet/streptozotocin-induced DN rat model was established to evaluate the renoprotective effects of SAA in vivo. Renal function, histopathological alterations, inflammatory responses, oxidative stress, mitochondrial homeostasis, autophagy-related proteins, and macrophage polarization were assessed. Molecular docking was performed to validate the interactions between SAA and key target proteins.
RESULTS: SAA significantly improved renal function and attenuated histopathological injury in DN rats. In addition, SAA reduced oxidative stress, suppressed inflammatory responses, restored mitochondrial homeostasis, and inhibited M1 macrophage polarization. Integrated network pharmacology and proteomic analyses identified the PI3K/Akt/mTOR signaling pathway as a critical target of SAA, which was further supported by molecular docking and experimental validation. Mechanistically, SAA inhibited PI3K/Akt/mTOR activation and restored autophagy-related signaling, thereby alleviating renal injury in DN.
CONCLUSION: SAA exerts renoprotective effects against DN through modulation of PI3K/Akt/mTOR-mediated autophagy and macrophage polarization, leading to attenuation of oxidative stress, inflammatory responses, mitochondrial dysfunction, and macrophage polarization. These findings provide mechanistic insights into the therapeutic potential of SAA and support its further development as a candidate treatment for DN.

articles.title: Phytocannabinoid cannabidiol (CBD) in neurodegenerative diseases: From polypharmacology to drug development.
articles.abstract: Cannabidiol (CBD) is a non-intoxicating phytocannabinoid that has attracted interest as a multi-target neurotherapeutic candidate for neurodegenerative diseases. CBD is a lipophilic terpenophenolic chemotype whose phenolic redox chemistry, membrane partitioning, cytochrome P450-mediated metabolism, and formulation-dependent exposure are central to its biological activity and translational limitations. In addition, CBD engages a broad target network relevant to neurodegeneration. Major components include cannabinoid receptors, transient receptor potential channels, peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor-γ, adenosine and serotonin signaling systems, voltage-gated calcium channels, and redox-regulatory pathways. These mechanisms converge on neuroinflammation, excitotoxicity, mitochondrial dysfunction, impaired proteostasis, and synaptic injury. Preclinical studies across models of Alzheimer's disease, Parkinson's disease, multiple sclerosis, Huntington's disease, and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis consistently support CBD's anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, mitochondria-protective, and neuroprotective pharmacology. The magnitude of these effects depends on dose, treatment timing, model system, and route of administration. Clinical evidence remains preliminary and is mainly symptomatic, with signals in agitation, sleep disturbance, spasticity, quality of life, and neuropsychiatric symptoms rather than proven disease modification. Key barriers to development include low and variable oral bioavailability, incomplete brain exposure data, uncertain active metabolite contributions, limited target-engagement biomarkers, and insufficient exposure-response definition. Future development of CBD and optimized cannabinoid-derived analogues will require medicinal chemistry strategies to improve potency, selectivity, metabolic stability, CNS exposure, and formulation performance. Parallel biomarker-driven clinical trials are needed to define pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic relationships and evaluate disease-modifying potential.

articles.title: Discovery of a brain penetrant NLRP3 inflammasome inhibitor that reduces neuropathic pain in mice.
articles.abstract: In our continuing campaign to discover novel inhibitors of the nucleotide-binding oligomerization domain (NOD)-like receptor (NLR) protein 3 (NLRP3), an emerging drug target that tightly regulates the innate immune responses, a 1H-1,2,3-triazole-4-carboxamide scaffold was designed and optimized. Iterative optimization led to the identification of a lead inhibitor, 22, with an IC50 of 70 nM to suppress the release of interleukin (IL)-1β upon NLRP3 activation. Further in vivo studies supported its selective suppression of the NLRP3 inflammasome. Pharmacokinetic studies of 22 and PET imaging studies employing a F-18 tracer of 22 demonstrated 22 as a brain penetrant with reversible binding kinetics within the CNS. Importantly, treatment of AD patient-derived hiPSC glia cells including microglia and astrocytes and neuropathic pain mice with 22 led to suppression of NLRP3 expression and decreased pain and pain-like behavior, supporting the translational promise of this compound and analogs from this chemotype.

articles.title: 3D-printed fish-skin-derived composite dECM hydrogel patch for immunomodulatory and pro-angiogenic diabetic wound repair.
articles.abstract: Diabetic wounds are sustained by persistent inflammation, oxidative stress, infection susceptibility, and impaired angiogenesis, highlighting the need for bioactive dressings with manufacturable architectures. Here, we developed a methacrylation-free and photopolymerization-free fish-derived composite decellularized extracellular matrix (dECM) hydrogel scaffold by blending tilapia skin-derived dECM (TdECM) with carp skin-derived dECM (CdECM). Rheology-guided screening identified TdECM/CdECM-2, a 1:2 (v/v) blend of TdECM and CdECM, as a printable formulation that combined shear-thinning behavior, thermally induced collagen fibrillogenesis, and extrusion printability. Post-print stabilization with 1-ethyl-3-(3-dimethylaminopropyl)carbodiimide (EDC) and N-hydroxysuccinimide (NHS) preserved lattice architecture and generated highly porous scaffolds with a porosity of 90.3 ± 3.9%. In vitro, the composite scaffold (TdECM/CdECM-2) supported fibroblast, keratinocyte, and endothelial cell growth; promoted keratinocyte migration and endothelial network formation; and reduced Staphylococcus aureus and Pseudomonas aeruginosa survival to 10.5 ± 1.3% and 13.3 ± 3.3%, respectively, in direct-contact assays. Macrophage studies indicated attenuated pro-inflammatory gene expression, increased pro-regenerative macrophage-associated markers, and reduced oxidative stress-associated reactive oxygen species accumulation. In mice with streptozotocin-induced diabetes, TdECM/CdECM-2 increased wound closure to 91.2 ± 3.9% at day 14, compared with 73.2 ± 9.7% in the untreated control and 79.3 ± 12.5% in the porcine skin-derived dECM (PdECM) group, together with improved re-epithelialization, collagen deposition, and cluster of differentiation 31 (CD31)-positive neovascularization, and reduced inflammatory myeloid cell accumulation and macrophage activation. Exploratory single-cell transcriptomic profiling suggested treatment-associated modulation of immune and stromal/endothelial gene programs related to inflammation and angiogenesis. These findings support fish-derived composite dECM scaffolds as printable bioactive wound dressing platforms for diabetic wound repair.

articles.title: Silymarin attenuates neuroinflammation after subarachnoid hemorrhage by inducing M2 microglial polarization via activation of the JAK1/STAT6 signaling pathway.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Neuroinflammation represents a key pathological process in early brain injury (EBI) following subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH) and contributes significantly to poor outcomes. Silymarin, known for its anti-inflammatory and antioxidant activities, has been shown to exert neuroprotective effects. Nevertheless, the molecular mechanisms underlying these effects remain to be clarified. An in vivo endovascular perforation model and an in vitro hemoglobin-stimulated model were used to investigate the pharmacological effects of silymarin in SAH. Neurological function was assessed using SAH scores and neurobehavioral scores. Neuronal apoptosis was evaluated by TUNEL staining. Neuroinflammation was measured by ELISA or qPCR, and microglial polarization status was determined by assessing CD86 and CD206 expression via Western blotting (WB) or immunofluorescence (IF) staining. Ruxolitinib and AS1517499 were applied to block the JAK1/STAT6 pathway. Silymarin attenuated early brain injury (EBI) after SAH, as indicated by improved neurological scores, reduced neuronal apoptosis, and lower brain water content. In vivo, silymarin treatment was associated with JAK1/STAT6 activation, elevated M2 markers, and decreased pro‑inflammatory cytokines. In vitro, silymarin activated the JAK1/STAT6 pathway, promoted M2 microglial polarization, and suppressed inflammatory cytokine production. In addition, pharmacological blockade of JAK1/STAT6 reversed silymarin's protective effects, confirming a causal role of this pathway in the cellular context. Our in vitro data demonstrate that silymarin directly stimulates JAK1/STAT6 to drive M2 polarization and anti‑inflammatory responses. In vivo, we observed a correlation between pathway activation and neuroprotective benefits. Together, these findings provide a rationale for further exploring silymarin‑based therapies in SAH.
SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1007/s10616-026-01073-w.

articles.title: A biomimetic gas-protein co-delivery nanoplatform targets mitochondrial stress and GSDME activation for glioblastoma immunotherapy.
articles.abstract: Glioblastoma (GBM) remains one of the most aggressive primary brain malignancies, with the therapeutic efficacy of conventional treatments and cancer immunotherapy being severely hindered by the blood-brain barrier (BBB) and the highly immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME). Although pyroptosis, an inflammatory form of programmed cell death, can elicit potent antitumor immunity through the release of damage-associated molecular patterns (DAMPs), the precise induction of pyroptosis and the amplification of its immunostimulatory effects remain major challenges. Herein, we developed a biomimetic microglial cell membrane-coated nanosystem (M@GM) that integrates brain-targeted delivery, mitochondria-mediated damage, and innate immune activation for cascade-enhanced glioblastoma therapy. The nanosystem consists of a manganese carbonyl (MnCO) core loaded with Gasdermin E (GSDME) and cloaked with a microglial cell membrane, enabling efficient BBB penetration and active GBM targeting. Upon accumulation within the tumor microenvironment, M@GM responsively releases CO, Mn2+, and GSDME. CO and Mn2+ induced mitochondrial stress and ROS accumulation, which were accompanied by activation of the Caspase-3/GSDME axis and pyroptosis-associated cell death. The associated HMGB1 release and CRT exposure are consistent with an immunogenic cell death (ICD)-related response, while Mn2+ cooperatively activates the cGAS-STING innate immune pathway, promoting dendritic cell maturation, effector T-cell infiltration, and M1 polarization of tumor-associated macrophages, ultimately converting the immunologically "cold" GBM microenvironment into an immune-active "hot" phenotype. Both in vitro and in vivo studies demonstrated enhanced BBB transport and brain accumulation of M@GM, significantly inhibited GBM progression, prolonged the survival of tumor-bearing mice, and exhibited favorable biosafety. This work presents a biomimetic therapeutic strategy based on "biomimetic delivery-pyroptosis amplification-immune remodeling", providing a promising design paradigm for brain-targeted nanomedicine-enabled cancer immunotherapy.

articles.title: Protopanaxadiol-type ginsenosides ameliorate PTSD-like memory impairment and neuroinflammation in rats via suppression of TLR4/NF-κB signaling.
articles.abstract: Post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) is a serious psychiatric condition that develops after exposure to intense or traumatic stress. Ginsenosides, the primary bioactive compounds of ginseng, have been reported to enhance cognitive performance. Protopanaxadiol (PD) and protopanaxatriol (PT) are two major classes of triterpenoid saponins. In the present study, a PTSD-like rat model was established using the single prolonged stress (SPS) paradigm, and the effects of PD and PT on memory dysfunction were evaluated. After SPS exposure, male rats received daily intraperitoneal administration of PD (10 or 20 mg/kg) or PT (10 and 20 mg/kg) for 14 days. PD treatment significantly improved both spatial and cognitive memory compared with PT treatment. PD also suppressed the elevation of pro-inflammatory cytokines in the prefrontal cortex and hippocampus, and mitigated the reduction in brain-derived neurotrophic factor mRNA expression in the hippocampus. In addition, PD attenuated the upregulation of Toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4) and nuclear factor (NF)-κB protein expression in the hippocampus. By contrast, PT treatment did not produce meaningful changes in memory performance or inflammatory markers. These findings suggest that the beneficial effects of PD are associated with anti-inflammatory activity that may involve modulation of the TLR4/NF-κB signaling pathway.

articles.title: Galectin-3 accelerates the progression of cerebral infarction by regulating the ERK/ROS/BRD4-mediated P2X7R/MerTK balance in microglia.
articles.abstract: This study demonstrates that Galectin-3 (Gal3) exacerbates cerebral infarction progression by modulating the P2X7R/MerTK equilibrium in microglia via the ERK/BRD4/HIF1α signaling axis, with reactive oxygen species (ROS) serving as a potential intermediate mediator linking ERK activation to BRD4 upregulation based on prior literature evidence. Single-cell transcriptomic analysis revealed that ischemia drives microglia from a homeostatic state to an activated disease phenotype, and virtual Gal3 knockout predicted corresponding downregulation of BRD4. Using a rat model of cerebral infarction, we found that the Gal3 inhibitor TD-139 significantly reduced infarct volume, promoted M2 polarization of microglia, and improved neurological function in behavioral assays. Mechanistic investigations in BV2 microglia revealed that Gal3 activates ERK1/2, leading to ROS accumulation, BRD4 upregulation, and subsequent HIF1α-mediated P2X7R transcription, while suppressing KLF4 and MerTK. This cascade increased P2X7R expression and suppressed MerTK/KLF4 expression, generating a pro-inflammatory and pro-apoptotic microenvironment. Notably, pharmacological inhibition of Gal3 enhanced efferocytosis and reduced apoptosis, whereas P2X7R blockade exerted similar neuroprotective effects. These findings identify Gal3 as a key regulator of microglial polarization via the experimentally validated ERK/BRD4/HIF1α-P2X7R signaling cascade, where P2X7R activation concurrently triggers cGAS-STING-mediated pro-inflammatory/pyroptotic responses and suppresses the KLF4/MerTK efferocytosis axis. Targeting this regulatory network could provide therapeutic benefits in cerebral infarction by shifting microglia toward the neuroprotective M2 phenotype and facilitating inflammation resolution. articles.title: Quality by design-assisted development of an intranasal Shikonin-loaded Mucoadhesive microemulsion for enhanced brain delivery: optimization, characterization, and Pharmacodynamic evaluation in a schizophrenia model.
articles.abstract: The present study aimed to develop and optimize a shikonin-loaded mucoadhesive microemulsion for intranasal delivery with the objective of improving nasal residence and facilitating central drug delivery. Shikonin is a naturally occurring naphthoquinone derivative with reported anti-inflammatory and neuroprotective properties. A Quality by Design (QbD)-based strategy was employed to establish a robust formulation with defined critical quality attributes and improved nasal delivery characteristics. Solubility screening identified castor oil, Tween 80, and propylene glycol as the most suitable oil, surfactant, and co-surfactant, respectively. Pseudoternary phase diagram studies facilitated the selection of an optimal microemulsion region, and formulation optimization was performed using a Box-Behnken design by evaluating the effects of oil concentration, Smix concentration, and sonication time on critical quality attributes. The optimized formulation consisted of 10% oil, 30% Smix, and 10 min sonication time, producing nanosized droplets with a particle size below 100 nm, a polydispersity index below 0.30, a positive zeta potential of approximately +30 mV, and entrapment efficiency exceeding 85%. Chitosan was incorporated as a mucoadhesive polymer to increase formulation viscosity and interaction with the nasal mucosa, thereby promoting prolonged nasal residence and potentially facilitating drug absorption. The resulting formulation exhibited markedly increased viscosity and mucoadhesive strength, confirming improved nasal retention. Transmission electron microscopy confirmed the formation of uniformly distributed spherical nanodroplets. The optimized shikonin-loaded mucoadhesive microemulsion exhibited significantly improved in vitro drug release (87.3 ± 1.25% at 8 h) compared with the plain shikonin solution (69.2 ± 1.63%). Ex vivo permeation studies across sheep nasal mucosa demonstrated superior permeation from shikonin-loaded mucoadhesive microemulsion (91.2 ± 0.41%) relative to the drug solution (73.27 ± 0.14%), accompanied by higher steady-state flux and apparent permeability coefficient values. In ketamine-induced schizophrenia-like behavioral model rats, intranasal shikonin-loaded mucoadhesive microemulsion significantly reduced hyperlocomotion, improved motor coordination, and attenuated cataleptic behavior relative to the disease control group. Orally administered chlorpromazine was included as a pharmacological reference treatment; however, the findings were not interpreted as evidence of route-equivalent or therapeutic equivalence between the two treatments. Histopathological analyses of cortical and hippocampal tissues revealed preservation of neuronal architecture and attenuation of ketamine-associated tissue alterations. Collectively, these findings provide preliminary evidence supporting the potential of the optimized intranasal shikonin-loaded mucoadhesive microemulsion for central delivery and modulation of schizophrenia-like behavioral abnormalities. However, the formulation was evaluated at laboratory scale, and pilot-scale/large-scale manufacturing feasibility and scale-up validation remain to be established before further translational development.
